method: The plan is hexagonal: cells tile in clusters of N cells, and a cluster tessellates only when N = i² + i·j + j² for whole offsets i and j, so N can be 1, 3, 4, 7, 9, 12, 13 or 19 and never 2, 5, 6 or 8. The offsets also locate the nearest co-channel cell: move i cells along a chain of hexagons, turn 60 degrees and move j more. The nearest co-channel cells sit at the reuse distance D = R·√(3N) from the serving cell, so Q = D/R = √(3N) is the co-channel reuse ratio and 1/N is the frequency reuse factor. With equal-power base stations, a pure distance power law and the first tier of co-channel cells all at the same distance D, the cell-edge signal-to-interference ratio is S/I = (D/R)^n / i₀ = (√(3N))^n / i₀, with n the path-loss exponent (2 to 6, typically 3 to 4 in a city) and i₀ the first-tier interferers the cell or sector sees: 6 for an omnidirectional cell, 2 with 120-degree sectoring, 1 with 60-degree sectoring. Where i = j (N = 3, 12, ...) some texts count one more, 3 against 120 degrees and 2 against 60 degrees; the page uses 6/2/1 throughout and says so on the page. It reports N, 1/N, Q, D for the entered cell radius, S/I in dB, the margin against the target (18 dB is the classic AMPS figure) and the channels per cell as total/N rounded down with the remainder. A worked default: i = 2 and j = 1 give N = 7 and Q = 4.583, so at n = 3.5 with six interferers S/I = 15.36 dB and the 7-cell plan falls 2.64 dB short of 18 dB, while at n = 4 the same plan reaches 18.66 dB, the textbook AMPS result. The table lists every tessellating N from 1 to 19 at the same exponent and interferer count, so the smallest cluster that clears the target is visible without trial and error. Inputs are bounded: i 0 to 20, j 0 to 20 and not both zero, n 2 to 6, cell radius 0.1 to 100 km, 1 to 10,000 channels and a target of 0 to 40 dB. Rounding: reuse ratio 4 decimals, distance 3, S/I and margin 2, reuse factor percentage 1. This is the standard first-tier hexagonal estimate and it is optimistic against a worst-case geometry, where the nearest interferers sit at D − R rather than D; it assumes equal cell sizes and powers, a single propagation slope with no breakpoint, flat terrain, no buildings or foliage, no adjacent-channel interference and idealised sector patterns. Channels per cell is raw division before any trunking loss, so pair it with an Erlang B or C calculation for offered traffic, and remember sectoring trades trunking efficiency for interference. It plans a reuse pattern; it does not allocate channels, model real interference levels or authorise spectrum. Everything runs locally in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
